macro_blurb: US equities closed lower as the AI-driven rally lost momentum, with sentiment further weighed down by disappointing forward guidance from Netflix in the streaming sector despite in-line revenue and profit growth. On the policy front, Senator Rounds signaled approval of Kevin Warsh's tone in his first testimony as Fed chairman, offering an early read on the incoming leadership at the US central bank. In Germany, Evonik CEO Kullmann publicly called for postponing the coal phase-out, reviving debate over the country's energy transition and its cost pressures on industrials. Additional US-specific noise came from Trump Media's plan to monetize premium access to the president's social posts and softness flagged in the US summer housing market.
synthesis:
Today's screen is a pure value-and-yield expression, and it is entirely American. All 10 picks are US-listed, average Value percentile sits at 89.4 and Yield at 88.4, while Quality trails badly at 53.0 — this is a cheapness-and-carry basket, not a compounder basket. Sector distribution is unusually flat: Consumer Defensive, Utilities, Consumer Cyclical and Basic Materials each contribute two names, with single entries from Technology (HPQ) and Healthcare (CNC). Composite scores compress into a tight 74.5–87.3 band, meaning no single conviction standout — the screen is telling us breadth in deep value, not a concentrated bet.

Three threads run through this. First, the regulated-utility rerating: ES and EIX both clear the 87th percentile on Value with dividend yields of 4.27% and 4.58% against a 3.15% sector median, and both carry debt/equity well above peer medians (182 and 226) — a rate-sensitive trade that Warsh's arrival at the Fed makes newly interesting. Second, the broken-brand yield trade: MO (6.01%), KHC (6.29%) and IP (5.04%) all screen top-decile on Yield but with either negative ROE (KHC -12.6%, IP -16%) or unreported quality — cash returns funded by contracting franchises. Third, HPQ and BBY share an old-tech-hardware value angle at 8.9x and 15.8x earnings, both leaning on AI-PC and RGB TV narratives.

The outlier is CNC — a 67% three-month rally paired with -26% ROE fits nothing else here. The conspicuous absence is louder: zero Financials, Industrials, Energy, Real Estate or Communication Services out of 275 scored names, and only one Tech pick as the AI rally cools. Watch Warsh's follow-up testimony and any escalation in the Eaton Fire claims against EIX — either can flip this basket inside two weeks.
